solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The main picture?

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open ocean, so a picture of the main is a painting of the ocean

explanation.surface: A question about which picture is the chief one in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'chief', but here it is the ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view of the ocean is a marine picture, the sense the cryptic reading gives.

clue.text: Country mansion let out in American port

parts.note: a seat is a large country house of a landed family

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand country house is rented out in a US harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Washington State city on Puget Sound is a major Pacific seaport.

clue.text: A crop that is produced by a tree

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A tree yields a harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'something produced by a tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the nut of the oak is a seed grown by that tree.

clue.text: Shut those geese up and get to the point

definitions.meaning: silence the honking of the geese, taking cackle literally as their noise
to stop chattering and deal with the main matter

explanation.surface: A farmer silences noisy geese and then gets down to business.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: stop idle talk and come to the important business, here also literally silencing the birds.

clue.text: One learning this is part of the eye

definitions.meaning: the dark opening at the centre of the iris

explanation.surface: A student is taught that this is a component of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a schoolchild and the dark aperture in the iris.

clue.text: One in a suit in the Athenaeum, for example

definitions.meaning: one card of the black suit with the trefoil symbol, alongside spades, hearts and diamonds
the Athenaeum is a famous gentlemen's members' institution on Pall Mall in London

explanation.surface: A man in a business suit sits in a grand London gentlemen's establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in a suit' suggests a businessman; it is a playing card of one of the four suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A card of the trefoil suit has this name, and the Athenaeum is an exclusive members' association of that kind.

clue.text: Struck by illness, desperately do a will

indicators.note: desperately suggests the letters thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: Seriously ill, someone frantically writes a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: brought down or incapacitated, especially by sickness.

clue.text: Light vehicle that is full of listening devices?

definitions.meaning: a small light carriage or pushchair
bugs are hidden microphones, so a room full of them is wired for spying

explanation.surface: A small car crammed with surveillance microphones.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a light carriage or pram and, playfully, something riddled with bugs.

clue.text: Hot crab, ready cooked, that provides energy

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or messed with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hot crab dish, ready to eat, gives you a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'something that provides energy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars and starches are the nutrients the body burns as its main fuel.

clue.text: Concerned with a contest

parts.note: a bout is a contest, as in a boxing match

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a forthcoming match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a book concerned with birds is a book on that subject, regarding it.

clue.text: Reaching the highest area in old capital

indicators.note: the word area is placed inside the old name of the capital

parts.note: Peking is the older Western name for Beijing, China's capital

explanation.surface: A traveller reaches the highest district of a former capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to top out or hit a maximum, as a career or a fever climbs to its summit.

clue.text: Container not altogether minute

indicators.note: not altogether means the word is not given in full, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: minute, meaning very small, gives tiny

explanation.surface: A box that is not entirely small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' is the adjective (my-NEWT), not the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A can for food or drink is a metal receptacle of this kind.

clue.text: Rustic at first helping sick goat

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word helping

parts.note: sick means ill
a billy is a male goat

explanation.surface: A countryman first assists an ailing goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unsophisticated country person, especially from remote US mountain areas.

clue.text: Lure with some succulent ices

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tempt someone with juicy ice lollies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes letters from the end of succulent and the start of ices.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tempt or attract someone, as bait draws a fish.

clue.text: Haircut not raised, certainly

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: sure means certainly, as in a reply of 'sure!'

explanation.surface: A haircut that definitely did not go up.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the shaven crown worn by monks is a particular style of cut.

clue.text: Appear to embarrass

definitions.meaning: to arrive or turn up, as guests at a party
to make someone look foolish by outdoing or exposing them

explanation.surface: To turn up somewhere, intending to make someone feel awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to arrive and to humiliate someone by comparison.

clue.text: Ancient punishment, one bitter to swallow, or finally deadly

parts.note: a bitter pill to swallow is something unpleasant to accept

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of deadly

explanation.surface: An old punishment: one bitter dose to take, or else death.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the wooden frame locking head and hands in which offenders were publicly mocked.

clue.text: Was interested to follow cricket scores: be very nervous

indicators.note: to follow places the interest word after the scoring word

parts.note: runs are the units scored in cricket
to have cared is to have been interested

explanation.surface: A fan who followed the cricket scores ends up anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, points are called runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to act out of fear, panicking or behaving timidly.

clue.text: Step right up to summarise

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to come forward and give a summing-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go over the main points again briefly.

clue.text: Proportion found in peroration

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A sense of balance appears in the closing part of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: A peroration is the closing part of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the relation in size between two quantities.

clue.text: Slippery customer starts to explain: evident lies

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the following three words

explanation.surface: A shifty character begins to explain, telling obvious untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's slippery person is a fish in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake-like fish is proverbially hard to hold, so it is a slippery creature.

clue.text: Rowing team's bulk initially reduced

indicators.note: initially reduced means the word is cut at its start, losing its first letter

parts.note: weight means bulk or heft

explanation.surface: A rowing crew's heaviness was cut back early on.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat crew of this many oarsmen, plus cox, carries the name of its number.

clue.text: Top clue represented in lines of verse

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The best clue of the puzzle is written out as poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Two rhyming lines of poetry together form a pair of this kind.

clue.text: Violence in an attempt to capture king

parts.note: an gives the single letter A

indicators.note: to capture means the attempt word holds the king's letter inside it

parts.note: a go is an attempt
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on British postboxes

explanation.surface: Bloodshed breaks out during a bid to seize a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: King is GR here, Georgius Rex, rather than the single letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for aggressive trouble-making or fighting, short for aggravation.

clue.text: We hear aristocrat is a seaside attraction

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: Gossip says a nobleman is a big draw at the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure platform jutting into the sea, as at Brighton, is a classic British resort draw.

clue.text: Home in sacred surroundings? Well, really!

indicators.note: in places the home word inside the sacred word
surroundings says the sacred word wraps around the other

parts.note: sacred means holy
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A dwelling set within holy grounds prompts an exclamation of exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disapproval or exasperation, used just like the clue's outburst.
